title: Onramp microcopy, pricing framing & metric experiments
summary: Working doc collecting microcopy variants, quickstart angles, competitive callouts, and measurement ideas for the Hosted API onramp. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success for engineers, make cost expectations transparent, and surface messaging that reduces churn from unexpected bills.
objectives: 1) Ship a concise set of tested microcopy strings for UI, emails, and SDK README. 2) Provide 3 quickstart flows (curl, Node SDK, embeddings) with clear success signals. 3) Draft pricing language that balances simplicity with predictability. 4) Define 6 A/B experiments and their success metrics.
audience: Primary: Software and ML engineers evaluating Hosted API. Secondary: platform/product managers and solution engineers running demos with customer accounts.
key_messages:
- Developer-first: get from zero to a working request in < 5 minutes with sample data and predictable pricing examples.
- Production-economics: we give explicit levers (batching, cache, quantization recommendations) so you can trade latency & cost without surprises.
- Same API across hosted, dedicated, private: prototype on hosted, scale to dedicated/private.
- Transparent unit metrics: we surface tokens, egress, compute estimates and an estimated monthly cost preview in the Console.
microcopy_samples: CTA (quick): Try the Hosted API — 3 lines of code, 2 minutes to first token.
CTA (conservative): Start for free — includes 200k tokens and smart usage alerts so you never get surprised.
Console banner: Running low on free credits? Turn on cost alerts to pause traffic at a threshold.
Quickstart heading: First request in 90 seconds — curl, Node.js, Python examples below.
Error message (rate limit): You reached your realtime throughput. Try a smaller batch or enable burst capacity; learn more in docs.
Pricing teaser on homepage: Pay per token when prototyping, reserve capacity for predictable production pricing.
Help tooltip (batching): Batching groups short requests into one GPU pass — cheaper per token, slightly higher p50 latency.
Email subject (trial): Your Hosted API credits are active — ship your first feature this week
quickstart_angles: Minimal curl-with-secrets: single curl command that returns a completion; emphasize streaming preview. Success metric: first token received. Time goal: <= 2 minutes.

App seed (chat widget): drop-in 50-line widget using the Node SDK; includes sample system prompt and conversation state management with KV cache example. Success: local chat working plus Console observed token counts.
Embeddings walkthrough (search): index 50 docs using the SDK, run a semantic search with similarity threshold. Success: relevant search results, embedding cost estimate shown in Console.
Ops-first: demo switching to dedicated routing in Console (toggle) to illustrate predictable SLO and commit workflow. Success: view of throughput graph and cost delta simulation.
Risk-averse demo: enable quota and alerts, show rollback to smaller model variant automatically. Success: simulated traffic spike and graceful fallback logs.
Metric-first tutorial: show how to interpret per-token latency, per-request compute units, and monthly forecast in Console. Goal: reduce cognitive load — call out top 3 knobs to tune cost.
pricing_language_drafts_notes: (draft fragments below — intentionally short, put into UI A/B tests)
pricing_language_examples: Option A (simple): Pay-as-you-go. Billed per 1k tokens. Use free credits to get started. Reserve capacity for guaranteed throughput and lower committed rates.
Option B (predictability): Estimated cost per request shown before you send it. Switch to reserved capacity when your average monthly spend is predictable to get 20–40% unit discounts.
Option C (developer framing): Small usage is billed by tokens; when you need predictable latency and price, move to Dedicated — same API, guaranteed SLOs.
Console tooltip (billing): We show both token units and an estimated compute cost. Cost estimates assume your current model, sequence length, and batching settings.
Support blurb (billing): Need an invoice or custom contract? Contact sales for enterprise billing and private deployment pricing.
Price-example microcopy: "In this example request (200 tokens in, 800 tokens out) your estimated cost is ~X units; enabling batching reduces per-token cost by Y%."
competitive_notes: OpenAI: strongest developer mindshare and rich SDKs; perceived black-box pricing can surprise teams. Opportunity: emphasize predictable, observable unit economics and per-route insights.
Anthropic/Cohere: positioning around safety and model-family differentiation. Opportunity: highlight runtime optimizations and easy routing between variants for cost vs. quality tradeoffs.

Cloud managed endpoints (AWS/Azure/GCP): strong enterprise contracts and cloud integration. Opportunity: our unified API + private option is simpler for teams that want to move from prototype to air-gapped or VPC without retooling.
Self-host vendors: focus on control but require heavy ops. Opportunity: position Redwood as the middle path — high-performance runtime + ops-lite managed flows and optional private deployments.
Key differentiated claims to test: per-request cost preview, console-first observability, one-click fallback to cheaper model variant, and explicit batching/caching suggestions in the SDK.
experiments_and_metrics: 1) CTA A/B: 'Try in 3 lines of code' vs 'Start with free credits' — measure click-to-first-request and 7-day retention. Success: increase first-success rate by +15%.

2) Pricing microcopy A/B in Console: show 'estimated cost' vs 'no estimate' before running heavy batch — track rate of aborted heavy requests and billing disputes. Success: reduce aborted runs by 25%.
3) Quickstart mode split: show 'curl-first' vs 'widget-first' based on detected role — measure time to first meaningful dev action (code copied, request sent). Success: reduce median time by 30%.
4) Cost transparency test: show token+compute estimate vs tokens-only — measure number of users enabling alerts and number of billing support tickets. Success: lower support tickets by 20%.
5) Channel experiment: include 'dedicated savings' sentence in trial onboarding email vs control — measure conversion to sales-assist conversations. Success: +10% MQLs.
6) Microcopy severity test for errors: friendly retry copy vs technical error copy — measure user path-to-retry and churn in dev sandbox. Success: increase retries by 40%.
Metrics to instrument: first-request time, first-token latency, 7/30/90d retention, quota alerts enabled, billing disputes, demo-to-DOC conversion, MQL rate from trial.

- UX: run 5 quick guerrilla tests with external devs on the curl quickstart wording next week.
notes_on_tone_and_voice: Keep copy low-friction and slightly nerdy — assume devs appreciate precise speed/cost signals but don't want marketing fluff. Use concrete numbers and quick toggles (e.g., 'Enable burst capacity', 'Show estimate'). Avoid ambiguous adjectives like 'fast' without measurable context.
implementation_guidance:
- Ship microcopy variants as feature flags so we can A/B test without code releases.
- Add preflight cost estimate to Console run modal for any request that will cost > X credits.
- Instrument telemetry for 'estimate viewed' and 'estimate accepted' to link to billing outcomes.
- Create a small SDK helper 'redwood.previewCost(request)' that returns estimate objects for docs and UI demos.
